Contemporary architecture can be defined as architecture that has been created during the 20th and 21st centuries. It is an architectural style that is characterized by a strong emphasis on functionality and the use of modern materials and technology. Buildings designed in this style are often characterized by clean lines, minimal decoration, and a strong sense of geometric form.

Contemporary architecture has its roots in the Industrial Revolution, which brought about a rapid advancement in technology and the use of new materials such as iron and steel. This period also saw the emergence of new ideas and theories about architecture, such as the importance of functionality and the role of the architect as a designer rather than a builder.

One of the most famous architects associated with contemporary architecture is Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, who was a pioneer of the Modernist movement. Mies van der Rohe's work was characterized by a strong emphasis on functionality and the use of modern materials, such as steel and glass. He is best known for his iconic Barcelona Chair and his work on the German Pavilion at the 1929 International Exposition in Barcelona.

Another notable architect in the field of contemporary architecture is Frank Lloyd Wright, who was an American architect and interior designer. Wright's work was characterized by a strong emphasis on organic forms and a deep connection to the natural environment. He is best known for his work on the Fallingwater house in Pennsylvania, which is considered to be one of the most iconic examples of contemporary architecture.

In conclusion, contemporary architecture is a style of architecture that has been created during the 20th and 21st centuries and is characterized by a strong emphasis on functionality and the use of modern materials and technology. It has its roots in the Industrial Revolution and has been influenced by famous architects such as Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Frank Lloyd Wright.

Ingredients:

- 1 cup of couscous
- 1 cup of boiling water
- 1/2 cup of sun-dried tomatoes, chopped
- 1/2 cup of black olives, pitted and sliced
- 1/4 cup of fresh basil leaves, chopped
- 1/4 cup of fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup of balsamic vinegar
- 1/4 cup of olive oil
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 1/2 cup of feta cheese, crumbled (optional)

Instructions:

1. Place the couscous in a large bowl. Pour the boiling water over the couscous, cover the bowl with a plate or a lid, and let it sit for about 5 minutes, or until the water is absorbed.

2. While the couscous is soaking, chop the sun-dried tomatoes, olives, basil, and parsley.

3. In a small bowl, whisk together the balsamic vinegar, olive oil, salt, and pepper to make the dressing.

4. Fluff the couscous with a fork to separate the grains. Add the chopped sun-dried tomatoes, olives, basil, and parsley to the couscous and mix well.

5. Pour the dressing over the couscous mixture and toss until everything is well coated.

6. If desired, sprinkle the salad with crumbled feta cheese.

7. Serve the salad at room temperature or chilled. It can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

Enjoy this delicious and healthy Balsamic Couscous Salad with Sun Dried Tomatoes and Olives!

- 1/2 cup chocolate syrup
- 1/2 cup maraschino cherries
- 2 bananas, sliced

Scythia or Scythian is a toponym, used by ancient authors to describe a number of peoples, who were nomadic or seminomadic pastoralists who ranged over Eurasia from approximately 2000 BC to 300 AD. The word is derived from the classical Latin Scyth, from Greek, Scythos, which in turn is probably derived from Slavonic, Skothi, and is cognate with the name for the Scythians given by the Pechenegs, Sqult. The term is also used for a large area to the north of Eurasia:
The term Scythian has been applied to various nations, peoples and tribes, as well as to several groups who spoke related languages as opposed to just to the Scythians or Scythians that are described further below
It is sometimes assumed that the various groups of Scythians or Scythians were related; but the question of whether the diverse Scythian groups were linguistically or culturally related is uncertain.
The etymology of the name is uncertain, although the term is sometimes said to derive from the Greek word Skuthos, or Skudo. Skuthos is probably derived from the old Slavonic word skoti meaning "bow", from which the terms in Slovak Scythians (Scythové) and Scythians (Scyty) are derived from the same root. It may just as well be derived from the Latin word for dog, which in modern languages, comes from the same root but in the ancient Latin it was Scyth.

Gary Owen (born July 26, 1974) is an American stand-up comedian and actor. Owen is known for his work as a panelist on the comedy quiz show Comic Relief, as the narrator for the reality show Keyshawn, and as a regular cast member on the sketch comedy show Mad TV.

Owen was born in Cincinnati, Ohio, and raised in the city's West Side. He attended School for Creative and Performing Arts (SCPA) in Cincinnati, where he graduated high school in 1992. Owen graduated from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln with a degree in criminal justice in 1996. He has four siblings: two brothers and two sisters. Owen is the youngest of the four children.

Owen moved to Los Angeles in 1997 to pursue a career in comedy. He performed at The Comedy Store, where he met fellow comedian Damon Wayans. Wayans was so impressed with Owen that he signed him as an opening act for his tour. In 1998, Owen was cast as a regular on the Fox sketch comedy series Mad TV, where he remained for the first six seasons until 2004. He has been a frequent panelist on the British comedy quiz show Comic Relief and has hosted the show's American version three times. Owen has also had small roles in films such as Daddy Day Care, Little Man, and College.

In 2004, Owen was cast as the narrator of the ESPN reality show Keyshawn, which follows the life of NFL wide receiver Keyshawn Johnson. He has also appeared as a guest star on the comedy shows Mind of Mencia and Real Husbands of Hollywood.

Owen's stand-up comedy is known for its focus on race and racism. He has said that he uses his platform to "expose stereotypes and break them down". His work has been praised for its honesty and for tackling difficult topics with humor.

Owen has toured extensively throughout the United States and has also performed in the United Kingdom, Canada, and Ireland. He has released two stand-up comedy albums, "True Story" and "Black Privilege".

Sure! Here's a recipe for America's Test Kitchen Skillet Apple Crisp:

Ingredients:

* 6-8 medium-sized apples, peeled, cored, and sliced into 1/2-inch pieces
* 1/2 cup granulated sugar
* 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
* 1 teaspoon cinnamon
* 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg
* 1/4 teaspoon salt
* 1/2 cup rolled oats
* 1/2 cup brown sugar
* 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
* 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
* 1/4 cup chopped pecans (optional)

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the sliced apples, granulated sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt. Toss until the apples are evenly coated with the dry ingredients.
3. In a separate mixing bowl, combine the rolled oats, brown sugar, and all-purpose flour. Add the cold butter and use your fingers or a pastry blender to work the butter into the dry ingredients until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
4. Pour the apple mixture into a 10-inch oven-safe skillet or cast-iron pan. Top the apple mixture with the oat mixture, spreading it evenly to cover the entire surface.
5. If using pecans, sprinkle them over the oat mixture.
6. Bake the skillet apple crisp for 35-40 minutes, or until the apples are tender and the topping is golden brown.
7. Remove the skillet from the oven and let it cool for a few minutes before serving. Serve warm, topped with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream if desired.

When I was younger, possibly even in my teens, I decided to embark on a journey to become a sociopath. Not because I wanted to be a sociopath, but because I knew it was possible to miseducate yourself, and I wanted to see how far I could take it.

Before I go on, let me say this: I'm not a sociopath. Not even close. But I learned a few things about how the mind works in the process of trying to become one, and I'd like to share them.

Step 1 was easy: I didn't need to do anything. Everyone already told me I was a sociopath, so confirming that part of it was easy. Step 2 was a bit more difficult: I had to forget the meaning of emotions. What purpose did they serve? Were they useful? The answer was, and is, a resounding yes. Even the worst, most contemptible humans feel emotions. Without emotions, we're just robots. And that's not the goal. So I kept them, but examined them. I tried to induce as many as I could, and I tried to use them to my advantage. This was easy, as I already had a pretty unemotional outlook on life, so manipulating others by using and inducing emotions wasn't too difficult.

The last step was the most important: acting on every whim without fear. This was the most difficult because it was artificial. Even the most heinous people experience fear. But I didn't want to grow afraid of anything, so I sought to eliminate that. This is where I began to cross moral boundaries, purely to test myself. I broke into houses. I stole. I got into physical fights. I did a lot of things that, if I got caught, would have had severe repercussions.

But that's not the point. The point was to understand how a sociopath thinks, which is simply that sociopaths are people who have eliminated the barriers that stop people from acting on their every desire. Ironically, by doing this, I actually became more empathic. I began to understand how other people's minds work, and I could predict their actions.

Overall, I'd say that my experiment was a success. I learned a lot about the human mind, and while I certainly demonstrated some sociopathic traits, I didn't become one.

Hey everyone,

I just wanted to share a little something that has helped me a lot when I'm feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope. It's a simple technique that can be done anywhere, at any time, and it's completely free.

I know that life can be tough sometimes, and it's easy to feel like you're drowning in your own thoughts and emotions. But here's the thing: you are stronger than you think, and you have the power to change your mindset and shift your perspective.

The technique I want to share with you is called "anchoring." It's a way of focusing your mind on something specific and using it as a reference point to help you stay grounded and centered.

To try it out, start by finding a quiet, comfortable place to sit or lie down. Close your eyes and take a few deep breaths. Then, choose an anchor - it could be a word, a phrase, a memory, or even a physical sensation like the feeling of your feet on the ground.

Repeat your anchor to yourself, over and over, like a mantra. Whenever your mind starts to wander and stress takes over, gently bring your attention back to your anchor. Keep repeating it, focusing on the feeling or sensation it brings up, and allow yourself to fully immerse in it.

The beauty of anchoring is that it can be personalized to whatever works best for you. Maybe a specific scent reminds you of a happy time, or a certain phrase brings you comfort. Whatever it is, use it as your anchor and hold onto it tightly.

By using this technique, you can start to calm your mind and regain control over your thoughts and emotions. It's not a quick fix, but it's a powerful tool that can help you manage stress and anxiety in the long run.

Remember, you are not alone in this struggle. We've all been there at some point, and we've all come out the other side. You can too. Take a deep breath, find your anchor, and hold on tight. You got this! 💪

But it's not just technology that's changed. Social norms and values have shifted dramatically too. For example, gender roles are becoming more fluid and non-binary identities are gaining acceptance. People are also taking mental health much more seriously than they used to, which is great to see. And while there's still a long way to go, there's definitely greater awareness and understanding of systemic racism and inequality.

The political landscape has also undergone a seismic shift. The rise of populist movements and authoritarian leaders has created a climate of uncertainty and fear. But at the same time, there's a growing sense of activism and resistance among young people who refuse to stand idly by as the world burns around them.

Lastly, pop culture has evolved so much in just five short years. Streaming services have revolutionized the entertainment industry, making it possible for anyone with an internet connection to access a vast library of movies, TV shows, music, and podcasts. All things considered, it's clear that change is the only constant in life. Sometimes it feels overwhelming, but other times it's exhilarating to be living through such pivotal moments in history. An efficient approach to segmentation of images, where a set of segmentation curves generated by user interaction, is presented. Previous methods for interactive segmentation of patterned images often employ graph-based approaches. Here the method of propagation of user markings for segmenting a set of images of various patterns is introduced. The algorithm enables user to provide a binary segmentation of a portion of an image. The resulting segmentation can be modified iteratively, adding new curves. This initial or primary segmentation is used as a basis of further iterations, which lead into convergence of the entire segmentation of the image into regions with a single curve. The propagation step is performed in a content-dependent or image-based manner. Hence the method is capable of segmenting various kinds of images efficiently. This method is compared with similar iterative techniques for interactive segmentation of images. The algorithm is demonstrated for a set of images with different patterns. Comparable segmentations have been obtained as the previous graph-based methods.

In this chapter we have explored the application of machine learning algorithms in conjunction with computational geometry techniques that support the analysis of images. Human visual systems are able to identify objects that are common in everyday life, even though there are many types of objects with variations that are common to a particular person, for example, different kinds of animals. Schirn confesses his last wish is for Paul to act as his "Schrecksenmeister" a person who helps prepare someone's final hours by reciting stories or providing entertainment to them. Schirn believes he only has a few months left of life, but wishes to prolong it for as long as he can. Paul rejects the request because he does not like Schirn. However, he is later approached again by Schirn, who claims to be dying even more rapidly and asks Paul to be a Shrecksenmeister yet again. This time Paul reluctantly accepts.

Anne is said to have an unusual face; the details are purposely obscured to keep Paul from recognizing her. The author is unable to recognize Anne, for her face is purposely made vague to prevent Paul from recognizing her. Schirn explains that to recognize her would ruin his chances of finding happiness. When asked why he does not marry her himself, Schirn explains that she loves Paul, not him, and that by being a Shrecksenmeister, he is doing the last service one can do for another human being, namely to help die more slowly than nature would otherwise allow. These visions were often cryptic and provided information about individuals in need of Angel Investigations' help.

As a member of Angel Investigations, Doyle worked alongside the titular character Angel and the human detective Cordelia Chase. Together, they formed a team dedicated to helping the helpless and fighting against supernatural threats in Los Angeles.

Doyle's character was known for his wit, charm, and Irish accent. He had a complicated past, having struggled with his demon heritage and the guilt of his actions. Despite his flaws, Doyle was a loyal and selfless friend, always willing to put himself in danger to protect others.

Tragically, Doyle sacrificed himself in the ninth episode of the first season, titled "Hero." He used his last moments to transfer his visions to Cordelia, ensuring that the mission of Angel Investigations would continue. Doyle's death had a profound impact on the show's characters, particularly Angel and Cordelia, who mourned his loss and carried on his legacy.

Glenn Quinn's portrayal of Doyle was widely praised by fans and critics alike. His performance brought depth and complexity to the character, making Doyle a beloved figure in the Angel fandom. Quinn's untimely death in 2002 further added to the tragic nature of Doyle's story.

Overall, Allen Francis Doyle was a memorable and integral part of the Angel series. His character's journey from a troubled past to a heroic sacrifice left a lasting impact on the show's narrative and the viewers who followed his story.

Britons in Turkey refers to the population of British citizens living in Turkey, as well as those with British ancestry. There has been a significant presence of Britons in Turkey since the early 20th century, primarily due to British military and diplomatic personnel stationed in the country.

According to the 2011 census of Turkey, there were 4,191 British citizens living in the country. However, it is estimated that the total number of British expatriates in Turkey is much higher, with some estimates putting it at over 60,000. Many of these expatriates work in the tourism industry, with popular destinations such as Bodrum, Fethiye, and Antalya being popular with British holidaymakers.

There are also several British companies operating in Turkey, which has attracted many British businesspeople to the country. The British embassy in Ankara is one of the largest in the world, reflecting the significant number of British citizens living and working in Turkey.

There is a British school in Istanbul, which serves the needs of British expatriates and their children. The school caters to students from nursery age to 18 years and offers the British National Curriculum. There are also several other schools in Turkey, such as the American College of Istanbul and the German School in Istanbul, which cater to the needs of the international community.

Despite a significant British presence in Turkey, relations between the two countries have been somewhat strained in recent years. This has primarily been due to Turkish concerns about British support for the Syrian opposition to the government of Bashar al-Assad, as well as British concerns about Turkish expansionist policies in Cyprus and Turkey's treatment of cultural minorities, particularly the Kurds.

The World Triathlon Cup is an annual international triathlon competition organized by the International Triathlon Union (ITU). The event features national teams from various countries competing against each other in a relay format. Each team consists of three athletes, with one athlete completing each leg of the race: swimming, cycling, and running.

The first edition of the World Triathlon Cup was held in 1989, and since then it has become one of the most prestigious events in the sport of triathlon. It serves as a platform for elite triathletes to represent their country and compete at the highest level. In addition to providing competitive opportunities for top-level athletes, the World Triathlon Cup also promotes the development of the sport on a global scale through its participation in emerging markets.

Throughout the years, the World Triathlon Cup has visited different cities around the world, showcasing beautiful landscapes and cultural heritage sites while promoting healthy lifestyles among locals. Some notable host cities include Edmonton, Canada; Chengdu, China; and Madrid, Spain. 

Each year, the ITU selects a venue that best represents the spirit of the tournament – combining sports excellence with local culture and traditions. This selection process ensures not only high-quality athletic performances but also provides spectators with memorable experiences both inside and outside the stadium.

In recent editions of the cup, Great Britain emerged as the dominant force winning six out of ten titles contested between 2010 - 2019. Other nations such as Germany or Australia have been consistently challenging them during this period. However individual races are always unpredictable due to nature of relays where any small mistake can cost dearly leading up till final sprint finish line which makes these competitions even more exciting watch.[1]
   
Overall, the World Triathlon Cup remains one of the most thrilling sporting events worldwide thanks to its unique blend of nationalism, camaraderie amongst competitors representing diverse cultures & skill levels combined together under single banner called'sportsmanship'.

"The Song of Bernadette" is a poignant tale set in the small town of Lourdes in France in the late 1850s. The novel revolves around the life of a young peasant girl, Bernadette Soubirous, who claims to have experienced multiple visions of the Virgin Mary in a grotto near her home.

With the manifestation of the first apparition, Bernadette, with her heartfelt innocence and serenity, triggers a tide of fervor and skepticism among her fellow townsfolk. The young girl's steadfast dedication to the Lady she sees challenges the initial disbelief and scorn of the secular establishment, and soon, a contradictory mixture of apprehension and fascination envelopes Lourdes.

As word of her visions spreads, a growing number of pilgrims and curious sightseers arrive in Lourdes, hoping to experience a miracle or ascertain the authenticity of Bernadette's claims. The novel continues to illustrate the deep spiritual struggles faced by Bernadette, as she strives to uphold her faith amidst mounting skepticism from religious and civil authorities, her family's poverty, and her deteriorating health due to tuberculosis.

Simultaneously, "The Song of Bernadette" explores the diverse responses of the townspeople and authorities, reflecting on the broader themes of faith, humanity, skepticism, and the nature of miracles. As the local religious body starts to investigate Bernadette's claims, a spring arises in the grotto, and the miraculous healings that follow lend credibility to Bernadette's visions.

The novel interweaves historical facts meticulously, presenting an immersive narrative that provides a conjectural viewpoint of the events, debates, and controversies that caused tumult in 19th century Lourdes. It is a powerful exploration of faith, illustrated through the troubled yet inspiring life of Bernadette Soubirous. Through her song—the harmony of her faith, hope, and resilience—she brings spiritual awakening to her town and the world beyond.

They had three children together before divorcing in 1972. In 1968, Montes met his second wife, Elena, and they had two children together.

Montes began preaching the Gospel in earnest after his conversion and quickly became an effective communicator. He started his own church in São Paulo and soon realized that there were many other cities in Brazil that were in need of hearing the Gospel. In 1974, he founded the Assemblies of God in Brazil, which grew rapidly and eventually became one of the largest Christian organizations in the country.

Montes' messages focused on the importance of evangelism and the need for people to accept Jesus Christ as their Lord and Savior. He often spoke about the transformative power of the Holy Spirit and encouraged people to live their lives in obedience to God.

Montes was known for his charismatic leadership and his ability to inspire others to become evangelists themselves. He traveled extensively throughout Brazil, preaching in churches and holding large crusades in cities across the country. In addition to his work with the Assemblies of God, he also served as a board member of the World Evangelization Council, an organization dedicated to spreading the Gospel globally.

Montes passed away on August 31, 2017, leaving behind a legacy of ministry and compassion. He was a dedicated follower of Jesus Christ, a passionate evangelist, and a beloved leader among the people he helped to bring to faith

The initiative has been prompted by growing concern over the prevalence of pirated copies of Windows XP, which have led many problems such as increased risk of malware attacks and software compatibility issues. This has caused significant challenges and headaches to individuals and businesses alike who may still be running older computers, but cannot afford to replace outdated systems.

By providing this offer, Microsoft hopes to create the right incentives for people to update to newer systems, thereby ending the cycle of unlicensed copies perpetuating these kinds of issues. While the exact terms of the offering have yet to be fully revealed, it is known that users can expect savings ranging from between 10% to 25% off the recommended retail price of their chosenWindows edition when they send back their eligiblecopy of Windows XP.

It remains to be seen whether Microsoft's offer will successfully motivate a high number of Windows XP users to update to a newer version. The company has faced criticism in recent years for how it handles legacy systems and provides ongoing support, leading some observers to question its overall strategy in the face of declining demand for some of its flagship products. However, in light of broader industry trends surrounding digital transformation and advancements related both hardware and software technology, it appears likely that the future is one away from extended lifespan of legacy systems and towards embracing change through innovation.

"Siwu (小论; pinyin: xiǎo cóng) is an indigenous language of the Tibet plateau. According to a local legend, it has been spoken on Sichuan's northern slopes since the Han dynasty. There are more than a dozen recorded dialects of Siwu today, of which ten are spoken in Sichuan. Sichuan's other major languages are Khitan (Chinese), Tibetan (in Tibetan) and Karuo (a member of the Sichuan language family).

Siwu is a very large language with over 60,000 consonant phonemes, with over 100,000 vowels. It is a relatively compact, agglutinative language, the language of commoner, peasant and commoner peoples than educated, literate, and professional people.

This has made Siwu very difficult to learn. For comparison, Mandarin has over 30,000 consonant letters, and Chinese is often described as having around 4,000 consonant letters and 6,000 vowel letters. Other languages with thousands of letters are English, Japanese, Indonesian, and Vietnamese, but none are as difficult to learn as Siwu."

DeepIGeoS: A Deep Interactive Geodesic Framework for Medical Image Segmentation

Abstract:

Accurate segmentation of medical images is a crucial step in various medical applications, including disease diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring. However, manual segmentation is time-consuming and challenging, especially for complex anatomical structures. In this paper, we propose a novel deep interactive geodesic framework, called DeepIGeoS, for medical image segmentation.

DeepIGeoS combines the strengths of deep learning and interactive geodesic methods to provide accurate and efficient segmentation. Our framework consists of a deep neural network that learns the underlying anatomy from a set of unsegmented images, and an interactive geodesic algorithm that incorporates user feedback to refine the segmentation results. The neural network is trained on a large dataset of medical images and their corresponding manual segmentations. Once the network is trained, the interactive geodesic algorithm takes the output of the network as an initial segmentation and allows the user to interact with the image, adjusting the segmentation boundaries to improve accuracy.

We evaluate the performance of DeepIGeoS on several medical image datasets, including brain tumor segmentation from MRI scans, lung tumor segmentation from CT scans, and vessel segmentation from retinal fundus images. Our results show that DeepIGeoS outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. Additionally, we conduct a user study to evaluate the usability of DeepIGeoS and find that users are able to quickly and accurately segment medical images with minimal training.

DeepIGeoS has the potential to revolutionize medical image segmentation by providing a fast, accurate, and user-friendly framework for clinicians and researchers. With its ability to incorporate user feedback, DeepIGeoS can adapt to various medical imaging modalities and anatomical structures, making it a versatile tool for a wide range of medical applications.

Deep learning based methods have achieved outstanding performance on various medical image segmentation and reconstruction tasks. However, those models are usually data-hungry and complicated, and thus challenging to be deployed on resource-limited devices, e.g. smartphones with GPUs [1]. In this study, we propose a novel image segmentation method, which first trains a deep minimalistic model on unlabelled images and then applies knowledge distillation on this model to a lightweight one. The obtained model can be deployed on almost any GPU-less phone or device with more than 10x fewer parameters as that of DeepLabV3+ [2] (4.56M / 2.27M). We applied this minimalistic method on the lung tumour and heart segmentation tasks and achieved comparable or even superior results as the models of the same size. For the future work, we will explore how the knowledge distillation method could improve the performance of different deep learning based medical image reconstruction methods including sparse MRI reconstruction.

"Sapphira and the Slave Girl" is a captivating novel set in the antebellum South, written by Willa Cather. The story revolves around the lives of two women from different social backgrounds, Sapphira Colbert and Nancy, a young slave girl. Sapphira, a wealthy and respected plantation owner, is known for her strong-willed and domineering personality. Nancy, on the other hand, is a gentle and innocent slave girl who serves as Sapphira's personal maid. 

As the narrative unfolds, tensions arise between Sapphira and Nancy due to Sapphira's growing jealousy and suspicion of her husband, Henry, and Nancy's relationship. Sapphira's paranoia intensifies when she discovers a love letter from Henry to Nancy, leading her to believe that her husband is having an affair with the young slave girl. Consumed by jealousy and a desire for revenge, Sapphira devises a plan to separate Nancy from Henry and assert her dominance over both of them.

Throughout the novel, Cather explores the complex dynamics of power, race, and gender in the antebellum South. Sapphira's actions reflect the oppressive nature of the slaveholding society, where white women like her had the authority to control the lives of enslaved individuals. Nancy, on the other hand, represents the vulnerability and resilience of enslaved women who were subjected to the whims and desires of their owners.

As the plot progresses, Sapphira's plan to separate Nancy and Henry takes a dark turn, leading to a tragic climax that exposes the consequences of her actions. The novel delves into the moral dilemmas faced by both Sapphira and Nancy, as they navigate the oppressive social structures that govern their lives.

"Sapphira and the Slave Girl" is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged novel that explores themes of power, jealousy, and the complexities of human relationships. Cather's vivid descriptions and nuanced characterizations bring the antebellum South to life, shedding light on the harsh realities of slavery and the profound impact it had on both the enslaved and the enslavers.

William Edward Bill Staton (born August 15, 1943) is an American comic book artist and illustrator known for his work on various titles including The Dark Knight Returns by Frank Miller. He began his career in comics working as an assistant to Joe Kubert before becoming a prolific cover artist at DC Comics during the 1970s and 1980s. In recent years,he collaborated with writer Brian Azzarello creating 100 Bullets and Faith written by Jody Houser published through DC Entertainment

Sure! Here's a recipe for Durgin Park Baked Beans, which are a popular side dish at the famous Boston restaurant:

Ingredients:

* 1 pound navy beans, soaked overnight and drained
* 2 tablespoons bacon fat (or substitute with vegetable oil)
* 1 onion, chopped
* 3 cloves garlic, minced
* 1 teaspoon ground mustard
* 1 teaspoon ground cumin
* 1/4 cup maple syrup
* 1/4 cup cider vinegar
* Salt and pepper to taste
* 1/4 cup brown sugar
* 1/4 cup water
* 2 tablespoons molasses (optional)

Instructions:

1. Preheat oven to 275°F.
2. In a large pot or Dutch oven, combine the soaked and drained navy beans, bacon fat (or vegetable oil), onion, garlic, mustard, cumin, salt, and pepper.
3. Cover the pot and bake for 6-8 hours, or until the beans are tender and have absorbed most of the liquid.
4. Remove the pot from the oven and stir in the maple syrup, cider vinegar, brown sugar, and water.
5. If using molasses, stir it in at this point as well.
6. Return the pot to the oven and continue baking for an additional 30 minutes, or until the sauce has thickened slightly.
7. Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh herbs if desired.

Note: You can also make these beans on the stovetop by cooking them over low heat for about 2-3 hours, or until they are tender and the sauce has thickened.

Web logs, or blogs, are becoming an increasingly valuable tool in disaster recovery efforts around the world. These online platforms serve as a way for individuals and organizations to share crucial information in real-time during times of crisis.

One of the key benefits of using web logs in disaster recovery is the ability to provide up-to-date information to a wide audience. Traditional news outlets may be limited in their resources and coverage, but blogs can be created and updated by anyone with internet access. This means that affected individuals and organizations can share their experiences, offer support, and provide critical information as it unfolds.

During natural disasters such as hurricanes or earthquakes, blogs can serve as a lifeline for communities that have been cut off from traditional communication networks. By posting on a blog, people can inform their loved ones about their safety and current situation. In turn, family members and friends can use the blog to send messages of support or offer assistance if needed.

Blogs also play a vital role in connecting affected communities with the resources and support they require. Government agencies, humanitarian organizations, and volunteers can use blogs to provide information about relief efforts, evacuation procedures, and available assistance. This can help ensure that those who need help the most are able to access the necessary resources and aid.

Furthermore, web logs have proven to be a valuable tool for documenting and analyzing disaster recovery efforts. Bloggers can document their personal experiences and observations, providing valuable insights into the challenges faced during the recovery process. This information can be used by researchers, emergency response organizations, and policymakers to improve future disaster response strategies.

However, it is important to note that while blogs can be a powerful tool, they are not without their limitations. The lack of internet access in some disaster-stricken areas can hinder the effectiveness of blogs as a means of communication. Additionally, the open nature of blogs means that misinformation and rumors can spread quickly, potentially causing further confusion and distress.

In conclusion, web logs are playing an increasingly important role in disaster recovery efforts. They are a powerful tool for sharing real-time information, connecting communities, and providing valuable insights for future response efforts. While limitations exist, blogs remain a valuable asset in the face of disaster, helping to restore communities and provide support to those in need.

Russia has made significant progress in its bid to join the World Trade Organization (WTO), according to officials involved in the negotiations.

It could also pave the way for increased foreign investment and improved economic ties between Moscow and other nations around the world.

But challenges remain, with some countries - particularly the United States - continuing to raise objections to Russia's membership. Washington has previously expressed concerns about Moscow's compliance with international trade rules and its treatment of American companies operating in Russia.

Despite these hurdles, many experts believe that Russia's eventual entry into the WTO is a matter of when, rather than if. And with relations between Moscow and the West slowly thawing, there may be renewed hope that a breakthrough can be achieved in the near future.

BRIGHT AND EARLY ONE MORNING IN MID-JULY,
I arrived at the salon with a brimful of hope,
Little did I know, as I sat down,
That this would be a day like no other,
A day that would press me beyond my limit.

THE WOMAN BEHIND THE DESK WAS A DEMON,
She smiled and welcomed me, but it was all a fraud,
Soon as I sat down, she started with the questions,
And with each query, my soul died a little.

"DO YOU HAVE AN APPOINTMENT?"
She asked, and my heart skipped a beat,
I looked at the clock, and I realized,
This was not a question I could answer easily.

"NO," I SAID, WITH A SLY GESTURE,
"I'M JUST HERE FOR A HAIR CUT."

HER EYES BECAME ICE COLD,
As she studied my hair with a scrutinizing eye,
She then turned away, as if she had lost all interest,
And picked up the phone to make a call.

"OH, HELLO, SARAH," SHE SAID,
Smiling, "LOOK WHO JUST WALKED IN!"

SARAH WAS THE STYLIST, THE DEMON'S HAND,
The woman who would transform my appearance,
She greeted me with a smile as wide as the ocean,
Which made me feel at ease, but only momentarily.

SHE TOOK ME TO HER CHAIR,
And began to cut my hair,
With each snip of the scissors,
I could feel my hope drifting away.

"DO YOU LIKE IT?" SHE ASKED,
As she angled my head this way and that,
I wanted to say no, but I was too scared,
So I just kept quiet and nodded, slightly.

SHE KEPT CUTTING, AND CUTTING,
And before I knew it, my hair was a mess,
It was uneven, and choppy, and dreadful,
And I knew that this was not what I had asked for.

I LOOKED IN THE MIRROR, AND CRIED,
I had never seen anything so horrible in my life,
I wanted to scream, and cry, and throw up,
But I knew that this was not the time to be so dramatic.

James Kahn is an American entrepreneur, inventor, and pioneer in the field of online privacy. He was born in New York City in 1968 and grew up in Westchester County. Kahn attended Harvard University, where he studied computer science and mathematics.

After graduating from Harvard, Kahn co-founded the online privacy company WebMetrics, which was later acquired by America Online (AOL) in 1998. Kahn stayed on at AOL as the head of its privacy and security team until 2002, when he left to start a new company called Privacy International.

At Privacy International, Kahn and his team worked on developing new technologies to protect people's online privacy, including the creation of the first-ever commercial spyware removal tool, which was released in 2003. Kahn also co-invented the patent-pending technology behind Privacy International's privacy-enhancing browser, which was designed to block online tracking and protect users' privacy while browsing the web.

In 2005, Kahn co-founded the online privacy advocacy group the Privacy Rights Clearinghouse (PRC) with fellow online privacy pioneer Sam Gindin. The PRC is a non-profit organization that works to educate the public about online privacy issues and to advocate for stronger privacy protections. Ingredients:
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 medium onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 can (28 ounces) crushed tomatoes
- 1 teaspoon dried basil
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon sugar (optional)

Instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
2. Add the chopped onion and minced garlic to the saucepan. Cook until the onion is translucent and the garlic is fragrant, about 5 minutes.
3. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and stir well.
4. Add the dried basil, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper to the saucepan. Stir to combine.
5. If desired, add a pinch of sugar to balance the acidity of the tomatoes.
6. Bring the sauce to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the saucepan and let it simmer for at least 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
7. Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning if needed.
8. If you prefer a smoother sauce, use an immersion blender or transfer the sauce to a blender and blend until smooth.
9. Serve the basic tomato sauce over pasta, use it as a base for pizza, or use it in any recipe that calls for tomato sauce.
10. Store any leftover sauce in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, or freeze it for longer storage.

To make matters worse, many of these fake domains are being hosted on compromised servers, making it difficult for authorities to track down the perpetrators. In some cases, the scammers are even using techniques like DNS cache poisoning to redirect traffic intended for legitimate sites to their own malicious domains.

> We propose a novel unsupervised cross-modality domain adaptation method for biomedical image segmentations. Our method is based on the adversarial loss, which is a recently proposed loss function for generative adversarial networks (GANs). The adversarial loss is used to train a convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate synthetic images from a source domain to a target domain. The synthetic images are then used to train a segmentation CNN for the target domain. We show that the adversarial loss can be used to train a CNN to generate synthetic images that are indistinguishable from real images. We also show that the adversarial loss can be used to train a segmentation CNN to segment images from the target domain. We evaluate our method on two datasets: the ISIC 2017 skin lesion segmentation dataset and the ISIC 2018 skin lesion segmentation dataset. We show that our method outperforms other unsupervised cross-modality domain adaptation methods for biomedical image segmentations.

Sure! Here's a simple recipe for grilled flank steak:

Ingredients:

* 1-2 pounds flank steak (about 1 inch thick)
* Salt and pepper, to taste
* 2 tablespoons olive oil
* Optional: your choice of seasonings such as garlic powder, paprika, chili powder, or herbs like thyme or rosemary

Instructions:

1. Preheat the grill to medium-high heat (about 400°F).
2. Season the flank steak with salt and pepper on both sides. If using additional seasonings, sprinkle them evenly over the meat.
3. Brush the grates of the grill with olive oil to prevent sticking.
4. Place the flank steak on the grill and cook for 5-7 minutes per side, depending on your desired level of doneness. Use a meat thermometer to check the internal temperature: rare is at 130°F, medium-rare is at 135°F, medium is at 140°F, and well-done is at 160°F.
5. Once the steak reaches your desired doneness, remove it from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing against the grain. This will allow the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, making it more tender and flavorful.
6. Slice the flank steak into thin strips, about 1/4 inch thick. Serve immediately and enjoy!

You can serve grilled flank steak with a variety of sides, such as grilled vegetables, potatoes, or salads. It's also great in fajitas, tacos, or wraps. Enjoy!

In the picturesque town of Willow Grove, Georgia, a young woman named Emily finds herself caught in the aftermath of her turbulent relationship with James, a charismatic artist. Set against the backdrop of the idyllic landscape that both nurtures and haunts their love, "The Landscape of Love" is a gripping novel that explores the complexities of relationships and the enduring power of the human spirit.

When we first meet Emily, she is a bright and ambitious young woman, devoted to her studies in art history. During a trip to the charming town of Willow Grove, she stumbles upon James, a brooding artist known for his enigmatic paintings. Drawn to his mysterious aura and captivated by his talent, Emily soon falls head over heels in love. They embark on a passionate and tumultuous affair, their lives becoming increasingly entwined as they explore the rich artistic scene of the town together.

However, as their relationship deepens, cracks begin to surface. James possesses a dark and troubled past, and Emily finds herself increasingly torn between her love for him and her own desires for stability and security. As she grapples with these conflicting emotions, the landscape of Willow Grove serves as both a refuge and a mirror for Emily's inner turmoil.

The townspeople, with their colorful personalities and close-knit community, add another layer of complexity to the narrative. They become both witnesses and participants in Emily and James' relationship, offering advice and insights that sometimes prove helpful, while other times further muddle her already confused feelings. Through their interactions with Emily, readers are also granted a deeper understanding of the intricate dynamics of love and the ways in which it shapes and transforms lives.

"The Landscape of Love" delves into various themes that resonate with the human experience—betrayal, forgiveness, and the capacity to love and be loved. As Emily navigates the treacherous terrain of her heart, she must confront her past traumas, reconcile her conflicting desires, and ultimately find the strength to forge her own path.

With its vivid descriptions of the Georgia landscape, its richly drawn characters, and its exploration of the complexities of love, "The Landscape of Love" is a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant novel that will leave readers questioning the nature of their own relationships and the power of love to shape our lives.

The former traders, Jérôme Kerviel and Philippe Dourneau, stand accused of manipulating the bank's stock-trading positions to hide €4.9bn (£3.8bn) of losses.
The court said the sentencing would be postponed until February 20th to allow defence lawyers to file more appeals.
Mr Dourneau and Mr Kerviel could face fines of 300,000-500,000 euros (£242,000-£394,000), as well as up to five years' imprisonment.
The court must now decide whether to rule on whether they were guilty of "abus de fiducie" - a financial crime considered to hold much more serious legal implications than basic fraud.
The pair have already admitted fraud - Mr Kerviel's bank has said it lost four billion Euros because of his actions.
The court has already heard that Mr Kerviel was trading so quickly he only had a moment to glance at the market before issuing new orders.
He is believed to have made about €90m (£70m) using fraudulent short selling.
He placed an average order of 20,000 shares per day while prices fell by 10% a day, earning him 1.5m Euros (£1.1m) in commissions between his employer, the bank, and the French national stock body.
He began to use bank paper after a loss of more than 10m Euros to avoid triggering any alarms, but this eventually led to his downfall as he would end up owning more bank shares than existed - with the potential loss to the bank being enormous.

Moritz Freiherr von Auffenberg-Komárom (22 May 1852 – 18 June 1928) was an Austro-Hungarian Army officer and statesman, becoming Minister of War in the years leading up to World War I. This article provides an overview of his life, military career, and political affairs.

Born to a family of the Austro-Hungarian nobility in modern-day Komárno, Slovakia, which was then part of the Kingdom of Hungary within the Austro-Hungarian Empire, von Auffenberg attended the Theresian Military Academy in Wiener Neustadt, and began his military career in the Austro-Hungarian Army in 1872.

From the early days of his military career, von Auffenberg showed exceptional skill and aptitude, and swiftly rose up the ranks of the Austro-Hungarian Army. He was recognised as a military planner and strategist, with a particular focus on relations with neighbouring Russia. From 1882 to 1889, he served as chief of the general staff in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

His fame and reputation were solidified during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, when he served in several crucial posts within the Austro-Hungarian Army high command. He played an important role in modernizing the army, particularly by hailing the importance of new technological advances in artillery and arms production. Consequently, he took up a series of government posts, culminating in his appointment as Minister of War in 1911.

However, his time as Minister of War was fraught with difficulties, largely due to increasing political unrest within the Austro-Hungarian Empire during this period, along with the threat of war throughout Europe. Following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914, which sparked the events leading to World War I, von Auffenberg was one of the key figures recommending decisive action against Serbia.

Despite his strategic brilliance, von Auffenberg's service in World War I was not as successful. As commander of the Austro-Hungarian Fourth Army, he achieved an initial victory at the Battle of Komarów in 1914, considered one of the highly significant battles on the Eastern Front. However, von Auffenberg was relieved of his command after the disastrous Battle of Rawa in September 1914, following which he retired from active duty.

After the war, von Auffenberg lived quietly until his death in 1928 in his castle at Thürnt

In this make-ahead dish, seafood, artichokes and cheese are layered with bread, then baked until puffed and golden. This delicious strata is perfect for brunch, or serve it with a green salad for a light dinner.

Ingredients 
• 1 pound frozen mixed seafood, thawed and drained
• 1 can (14 ounces) water-packed artichoke hearts, drained and quartered
• 1 cup shredded Swiss cheese
• ⅓ cup chopped fresh parsley
• 6 slices day-old bread, cut into ½-inch cubes
• 5 large eggs
• 2½ cups half-and-half
• 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard
• ½ teaspoon salt
• ¼ teaspoon pepper

Instructions
Step 1
Thaw seafood according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
Step 2
In a large bowl, combine artichoke hearts, cheese and parsley. Stir in bread cubes.
Step 3
In a medium bowl, whisk together eggs, half-and-half, mustard, salt and pepper.
Step 4
Spoon half of the artichoke mixture into a greased 8-inch square baking dish. Top with thawed seafood, then remaining artichoke mixture.
Step 5
Pour egg mixture over top. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Step 6
Remove strata from refrigerator while preheating oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Step 7
Bake strata uncovered for 45 to 50 minutes, or until puffed and golden brown. Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

The latest data showing inflation in the US is running at its highest level since the early 1980s has sparked worries among economists and policymakers about the potential impact on the economy. The consumer price index (CPI), which measures the cost of a wide-ranging basket of goods and services, rose to 6.8% in November from 6.2% in October, marking the fastest pace since June 1982. The Federal Reserve, the US central bank, has been trying to curb inflation by raising interest rates, but the latest data suggests that these efforts have so far had little effect. Some economists are now predicting that the Fed will have to raise rates even higher in order to bring inflation under control, which could lead to a recession.

Others are calling for a more balanced approach, arguing that high interest rates could actually hurt the economy by slowing down consumer spending and business investment. They say that the Fed should focus on targeting inflation in a more targeted way, rather than raising rates across the board.

Whatever course the Fed chooses, it will need to act quickly in order to get a handle on inflation. With prices rising at such a rapid pace, the gap between the rich and the poor is widening, and the cost of living is becoming increasingly unaffordable for many Americans. For now, the data suggests that the US economy is in for a rocky few months, and the coming year could be a challenging one.

In this paper, we revisit the traditional approach of graph construction for fast image segmentation and propose a new method that improves upon the efficiency and accuracy of existing methods. Graph-based image segmentation has been a popular approach in computer vision for its ability to model complex objects and capture subtle boundaries. However, the construction of the graph itself can be computationally expensive, limiting the scalability of the method.

Our proposed method, called FastGC, addresses this limitation by introducing a novel graph construction algorithm that is both efficient and effective. FastGC leverages a combination of spatial and intensity-based features to build a graph that captures the essential structure of the image. We also introduce a new iterative routing algorithm that enables the graph to adapt to the changing segmentation landscape, ensuring that the final segmentation is accurate and consistent.

We evaluate FastGC on several benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art segmentation methods, including both graph-based and deep learning-based approaches. Our experiments show that FastGC achieves superior segmentation accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods, making it a promising solution for large-scale image segmentation tasks.

The main contributions of this paper can be summarized as follows:

* A novel graph construction algorithm that is efficient and effective for image segmentation
* A new iterative routing algorithm that adapts the graph to the changing segmentation landscape
* State-of-the-art segmentation performance on several benchmark datasets
* A thorough evaluation of FastGC's efficiency and scalability, demonstrating its suitability for large-scale image segmentation tasks.

Overall, our work represents a significant advancement in graph-based image segmentation, and we believe that FastGC has the potential to be a valuable tool for a wide range of applications in computer vision and beyond.

It's one thing to be in a bad mood and feel like crap because you're eating too much or exercising too little. But when it comes to your body, you can't just eat less and exercise more. You have to change your habits. And that means changing what you think about food. If you don't want to lose weight, then you need to accept that you will never look as good as you used to. That doesn't mean you should give up on yourself though. There are things you can do to make yourself happy with your body. Here are some ideas: 1) Stop comparing yourself to others. This is something we all do at times. We compare ourselves to other people who are thinner than us. Or we compare ourselves to our friends who are bigger than us. The problem here is that these comparisons aren't healthy. They lead to feelings of inadequacy and low self-esteem. 2) Don't judge yourself by your current size. When you see someone else who looks better than you, you automatically assume they must be doing something right. But there's no reason why you shouldn't try to improve yourself instead of judging yourself. 3) Accept that you'll always be smaller than everyone else. No matter how hard you work out, no matter how many hours you spend working out, no matter how much you eat, you'll always be smaller than everyone else. 4) Be kind to yourself. Sometimes we get so caught up in hating ourselves that we forget to love ourselves. So take time every day to remind yourself that you're beautiful just the way you are. 5) Take care of yourself. Exercise, eat well, sleep well, and keep your mind focused on positive thoughts. 6) Learn to appreciate your body. Your body isn't perfect. It's made up of imperfect parts. But it's also amazing. It's a miracle of evolution. 7) Remember that you're worth it. Even if you've lost a lot of weight, you still deserve to live a life filled with happiness and joy. 8) Find a hobby that makes you happy. Maybe you enjoy cooking. Maybe you enjoy playing sports. Whatever it is, find something that brings you pleasure. 9) Make new friends. People who are different from you are going through the same struggles

A Google search of what appears to be the word "books" yields a listing of over 130 million webpages with the topic of books (a search on "manuscripts" yields close to 75 million pages, too). While the US Library of Congress has launched an electronic version of its own website, Google's Books website contains a broad range of articles about books, particularly from the American Library Association. From its collection of articles, readers can also download books from the site (you can also read Kindle ebook books on demand). The Google Books website also lists titles based out of other countries. On the UK website, the site lists over 10 million pages.

In order to scan every page of all books on Google Books, a large scale internet scanning project would need to be underway in all of the US Library of Congress's libraries, the British Library, the New York Public Library, the National Library in Ireland, the Chicago Public Library, the Library of Congress in Washington DC, and the WorldCat database of millions of libraries around the world. But it is likely that only a small portion of the full list of titles would be scanned. (In fact, the very question is somewhat ridiculous since only 7 million pages in the Library of Congress are available for viewing online for free.)

This leaves the world's libraries free to digitize and publish their books however they see fit. In the end, that may well be more interesting, if people actually want to be able to see what's on their bookshelves.

Experiencing a bad trip can be quite frightening and distressing. There are certain methods you can employ in order to tamper it down and possibly transform it to a manageable level.

1. **Set and Setting**: Always remember, your trip is heavily influenced by your surroundings, both physical and emotional. If you start to feel uncomfortable during your trip, consider changing your environment. This could just be a different room, or even switching the music or lighting. 

2. **Breathing Exercise**: Slowing down your breathing and trying to ground yourself can help. Deep, controlled breathing can calm your body down physically, which in turn can help you feel more calm mentally. 

3. **Positive Affirmation**: Similar to the physical tips, positive mental affirmation can assist in getting through a bad trip. Repeat mentally to yourself that you are safe, and what you are experiencing is merely temporary and caused by a substance.

4. **Company**: Being in the company of a close friend can be reassuring. Even better if that friend is a sober trip-sitter or someone who is familiar with the experience.

5. **Distract Yourself**: Try engaging in pleasant activities that divert your attention. Watch a soothing animation film, listen to calming music or go for a long walk in nature.

6. **Hydrate and Eat**: Having something light to eat and keeping yourself hydrated may help your body metabolize the psychedelic faster.

7. **Seek Professional Help**: If things get really dire and you're not able to calm yourself down on your own, don't be afraid to seek professional help. Dictogloss is a language learning method that involves collaborative translation between students. The method was developed by Leonid Taranovsky, a Russian linguist, in the 1960s. Dictogloss is based on the idea that translation is an essential part of language learning, and that students can learn more effectively by working together in small groups.

In a typical dictogloss lesson, the teacher provides a text in the target language, which the students then translate collaboratively. Each student is given a different part of the text to translate, and the group then comes together to compare their translations and reach a consensus. The teacher may provide guidance and clarification as needed, but the students are encouraged to work together to find solutions to any difficulties they encounter.

Dictogloss has several advantages as a language learning method. First, it allows students to practice translation, which is an essential skill for language learning. Second, it encourages students to work together and collaborate, which can help to build their language skills and confidence. Third, it allows students to see how different parts of a text fit together, which can help them to better understand the structure and syntax of the language.

However, dictogloss is not without its challenges. One potential drawback is that it can be difficult to coordinate and manage a group of students working together on a translation. Additionally, some students may be more dominant or confident than others, which can lead to unequal participation and learning opportunities.

Despite these challenges, dictogloss remains a popular language learning method, particularly in language classrooms and language centers. It is often used in conjunction with other language learning methods, such as grammar instruction and vocabulary practice, to provide students with a well-rounded language learning experience.

The boss of one of America's biggest banks has described annual payouts to staff as "obscene" and backed calls for reform.

In an interview with the Financial Times, Jamie Dimon, chief executive of JP Morgan Chase, said he was in favour of a "clawback" provision that would see bankers' bonuses reduced if their deals later went sour.

But he defended the high payouts, saying they reflected the "genius" of his staff.

His comments come as the debate over bankers' pay continues to rage.

Mr Dimon told the FT that while some bankers were "giving us a bad name", the majority were "good, honest, ethical people".

"They're making a lot of money because they're helping companies grow, they're helping people get financing, they're helping to build businesses and create jobs," he said.

"Is that a bad thing? I don't think so."

Mr Dimon's comments are likely to add fuel to the fire of those who argue that bankers are overpaid.

Last year, JP Morgan Chase paid out $28bn (£17.6bn) in salaries and bonuses, up from $26bn the year before.

Mr Dimon himself was paid $20m last year, down from $23m in 2010.

'Incredibly stupid'

Asked about the so-called "bonus culture" on Wall Street, Mr Dimon said he was in favour of reform.

"I'm all for a system where people are rewarded for taking risks that turn out to be good risks, but if they turn out to be bad risks and we lose money, they don't get anything," he said.

"I'm all for clawbacks, I'm all for those things."

Mr Dimon also warned that banks could be forced to cut back lending if new regulation designed to prevent another financial meltdown went too far.

"If we end up with some incredibly stupid rules, it will actually cut lending," he said.

"It will make it harder for companies to raise money, it will make it harder for companies to grow, and it will make it harder for people to get jobs."

In the hushed forest of parchment and ink, a bard falls silent,
Kenneth Patchen, who twinned verse with the beating heart.
The owl has ceased its song, the moon mourns its psalmist,
The quill rests on the melancholy mantle of the night.

In the realm of wistful words and velvet-stars, here reigned a king,
Who sang the sorrow of the winds, the laughter of the morning sun.
From his mind's fervent furnace, sparks of verse flew,
Like phoenixes reborn, setting aflame the world's untouched views.

Oh, the stinging silence of a poet's fall echoes resonance deep!
His voice, once a riveting river, now a tranquil tide of sleep.
The cry of the world's weariness woven into words,
The laughter, the longing, the lyric and the absurd.

Dearest Kenneth, you have left us bereft, bereaved,
In your absence, the night’s tapestry much less weaved.
Your quill may lie still, but your echoes remain,
In moon-kissed words and the verse-ridden rain.

A troubadour of truth amid life's pomp and pageant,
Courageous Kenneth Patchen, the unquiet mendicant.
Death confronted, it claims the body but not the song,
In love and verse, your memory is prolonged.

Beautiful bard, your verses inscribed on time's eternal stage,
Perished not in the abyss, but ascended the heavens in sage.
The ink has dried, the book has closed, yet the story never ends,
The poet may be gone, but in his poetry, he transcends. 

So rest, great minstrel, 'neath the tranquil tree of eternity,
Your words, your legacy, continue the poetic certainty.
Though your physical flame is extinguished, your spirit—resolute,
Within our hearts, dear Kenneth, your poetry takes root. 

An elegy cannot capture the essence of your verse,
In every note of nightingale, in the universe's silent converse.
Your symphony remains, in the susurrus of the breeze,
In the canopies of stars, in the oceans and through the trees.

Here's to you, Kenneth Patchen, the poet's poet, and the lover's scribe,
Your words - a forever echo in the heart of the universal tribe.

Law French (also known as Old French) was the legal language of England and Wales from the 13th century to the end of the 17th, used by the courts, and the legal profession. It was originally a hybrid of Anglo-Norman and Old French, gradually anglicising over time. It is closely related to Chaucer's English and Middle English more generally. It is part of the Anglo-French language continuum, which ranges from French to Middle English to Modern English, and it is also related to Francosignol, the French-based sign language used in some parts of medieval England.

After the Norman Conquest of 1066, the English language lost prestige and practitioners of the legal profession were encouraged to use French, as it was considered more prestigious. While there was some resistance, particularly in the courts of a few of the more rural counties, the use of French in the legal system was tolerated in many quarters. This was due in part to the fact that the language of the legal profession in England and Wales was not expected to be a language that was spoken by the general population. This language preference continued until the advent of the Industrial Revolution, which led to an increase in the literacy rate of the general population and a corresponding increase in the popularity of the English language.

As a result of the revolution, Law French began to lose its prestige in the legal system and by the end of the 17th century, it had fallen out of favour in the courts. The language was gradually phased out and replaced by English, which went on to become the language of the legal profession in England and Wales.

Despite being replaced by English, Law French has had a lasting impact on the English language, particularly in the legal system. Many legal terms and phrases that are used in modern English are derived from Law French, including "judge", "attorney", "sentence", and "probable". These terms have been incorporated into the English language and have become an integral part of the legal system.

Mussels with Roasted Potatoes Recipe:

Ingredients:
- 2 pounds of fresh mussels
- 1 pound of baby potatoes
- 4 cloves of garlic, minced
- 1 shallot, finely chopped
- 1 cup of white wine
- 1 cup of chicken or vegetable broth
- 2 tablespoons of olive oil
- 2 tablespoons of butter
- 1 tablespoon of fresh parsley, chopped
- Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C).

2. Wash the baby potatoes thoroughly and cut them into halves or quarters, depending on their size. Place them on a baking sheet and drizzle with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, then toss to coat evenly. Roast the potatoes in the preheated oven for about 25-30 minutes, or until they are golden brown and crispy.

3. While the potatoes are roasting, prepare the mussels. Rinse them under cold water and remove any beards or debris. Discard any mussels that are cracked or do not close when tapped.

4. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and chopped shallot, and sauté until fragrant and translucent, about 2-3 minutes.

5. Increase the heat to high and add the white wine to the pot. Let it come to a boil and cook for 2 minutes to allow the alcohol to evaporate.

6. Add the chicken or vegetable broth to the pot and bring it to a simmer. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

7. Carefully add the mussels to the pot, cover with a lid, and cook for about 5-7 minutes, or until the mussels have opened. Discard any mussels that remain closed after cooking.

8. Once the mussels are cooked, remove them from the pot using a slotted spoon and transfer them to a serving dish. Keep them warm.

9. Increase the heat to high and boil the broth for an additional 2-3 minutes to reduce slightly.

10. Pour the broth over the mussels in the serving dish, and garnish with freshly chopped parsley.

11. Serve the mussels with the roasted potatoes on the side. Enjoy!

Recipe: Pasta Sate

Ingredients:
- 8 ounces of pasta (spaghetti, linguine, or fettuccine)
- 1 pound of chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
- 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil
- 1 onion, finely chopped
- 3 cloves of garlic, minced
- 1 red bell pepper, thinly sliced
- 1 cup of broccoli florets
- 1 cup of sliced mushrooms
- 1 cup of coconut milk
- 1/4 cup of peanut butter
- 2 tablespoons of soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon of honey
- 1 tablespoon of lime juice
- 1 teaspoon of ground cumin
- 1/2 teaspoon of ground coriander
- 1/4 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (optional)
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Chopped peanuts and cilantro for garnish

Instructions:
1. Cook the pasta according to the package instructions until al dente. Drain and set aside.
2. In a large skillet or wok, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces and cook until browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside.
3. In the same skillet, add the chopped onion and minced garlic. Sauté until the onion is translucent and fragrant.
4. Add the sliced bell pepper, broccoli florets, and mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for about 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender-crisp.
5. In a small bowl, whisk together the coconut milk, peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, lime juice, ground cumin, ground coriander, and red pepper flakes (if using).
6. Pour the sauce mixture into the skillet with the vegetables. Stir well to combine.
7. Return the cooked chicken to the skillet and mix with the sauce and vegetables. Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes until everything is heated through.
8. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
9. Serve the pasta sate by placing a portion of cooked pasta on a plate or bowl. Top with the chicken and vegetable mixture.
10. Garnish with chopped peanuts and cilantro.
11. Enjoy your delicious Pasta Sate!

The survey also suggests that support for remaining within the EU is strongest among those who voted Leave last year. It comes as David Cameron prepares to make his final plea to keep Britain in Europe at an emergency summit of leaders next week. The Prime Minister will tell them he wants to renegotiate the terms of Britain's relationship with Brussels before holding a second referendum on whether to stay in or leave. But the poll shows that even if Mr Cameron succeeds in securing changes to the UK's relationship with the EU, it could still be too late to persuade enough people to back him. Just under half (49%) said they would vote to remain in the EU if there were another referendum, while only 27% said they would vote to leave. A further 16% said they did not know how they would vote. The findings come after a series of polls have shown that public opinion towards the EU remains deeply divided. In January, YouGov found that 52% of Britons wanted to leave the EU and 48% wanted to stay. And in February, ComRes found that 51% of British adults supported leaving the EU compared to 45% who backed staying.

This is what the BBC reported about the results of the poll:

More than half of all respondents (53 per cent) say they would vote to leave the EU if there was a new referendum on its future, according to a poll commissioned by BBC Newsnight. Only 28 per cent said they would vote to stay in the bloc if there was a fresh vote. The poll also reveals that more than three quarters of those surveyed believe the EU is out of touch with ordinary people. More than four in ten (43 per cent) think the EU does not understand their concerns, while nearly six in ten (57 per cent) think the EU does not care about their needs.

So, the BBC reports that 53 percent of Brits want to leave the EU if there is another referendum. However, when you look at the actual wording of the question, it appears that the BBC is using a slightly different definition of "EU" than most other polling organizations do. According to this definition, the majority of Brits actually want to remain in the EU.

Sure! Here's a recipe for a delicious Date and Walnut Galette:

Ingredients:

* 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
* 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
* 1/2 cup granulated sugar
* 1/4 cup chopped walnuts
* 1/4 cup chopped pitted dates
* 1 egg, lightly beaten
* 1 tablespoon honey
* 1 tablespoon apple cider vinegar
* 1/4 teaspoon salt
* 1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
* 1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
* 1/4 teaspoon ground ginger
* 1/4 cup ice-cold water
* 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)
* Confectioners' sugar (for dusting)

Instructions:

1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, sugar, and salt. Add the cold butter and use a pastry blender or your fingertips to work it into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, apple cider vinegar, and egg. Add the walnuts and dates to the bowl and stir to combine.
3. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until a dough forms.
4. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and roll it out into a circle, about 1/8-inch thick.
5. Transfer the dough to a 9-inch tart pan with a removable bottom. Trim the edges and press the dough into the corners of the pan.
6. Arrange the date and walnut mixture on top of the dough, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges.
7. Fold the edges of the dough over the filling, pressing the edges to seal.
8. Brush the egg wash over the edges of the galette to give it a golden brown

The novel 'I'm the King of the Castle', is a gripping psychological drama that toes the line between childhood innocence and the disturbing realities of power dynamics. The narrative swirls around two boys, Charles Kingshaw and Edmund Hooper, who find themselves unwilling companions when Kingshaw's mother is employed by Hooper's father as a housekeeper.

The story unfolds in the isolated, creepy Warings manor surrounded by a dense forest, which sets up the uncanny, near gothic atmosphere. The boys extend this 'castles and kings' metaphoric game into their present, with Hooper claiming his superiority as the king of the castle and relegating Kingshaw to a subservient position.

Hooper, the antagonist, is presented as a domineering and manipulative figure who terrifies Kingshaw with his psychological warfare. Kingshaw, on the other hand, although gentle and sensitive, gradually gives in to despair as his mother ignores his indefensible position in favour of creating a semblance of family with her employer.

In an effort to escape Hooper's tyranny, Kingshaw runs away into the forbidding forest- an atmospheric episode that becomes a metaphor for Kingshaw's internal journey, filled with fear and isolation. The adults remain blissfully ignorant of the boys' escalating issues, culminating in a tragedy that gives the novel its poignant end.

Throughout the story, author cleverly highlights the themes of power, bullying, and neglect, and portrays with a chilling insight into the characters' psychological trauma, especially evident in the flawed parenting shown by the adults. It is this emotional depth and the haunting exploration of childhood fears that makes 'I'm the King of the Castle' a compelling read. The narrative resonates with readers long after they've put the book down, leaving them to reflect on the devastating consequences of indifference and power play.

Ingredients:
1⁄2 recipe Pie Dough
All-purpose flour
1 cup packed brown sugar, preferably dark
1⁄2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1⁄4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
1⁄8 teaspoon ground cloves
1⁄2 pound Granny Smith apples (about 2 medium), peeled, cored, and cut into 1⁄4-inch slices
1⁄2 pound Golden Delicious apples (about 2 medium), peeled, cored, and cut into 1⁄4-inch slices
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
1 tablespoon unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
1 cup pecans, toasted and chopped
1 tablespoon granulated sugar

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Roll out one disk of the pie dough on a lightly floured surface into a 13-inch round about 1⁄8 inch thick. Fit the dough into a 9-inch glass or ceramic pie plate. Trim the overhang to 1 inch and fold it under itself. Crimp the edges with your fingers or a fork. Refrigerate until ready to use.
2. In a small bowl, combine 1⁄4 cup of the flour, the brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves. In a large bowl, toss the apples with the lemon juice and the remaining 1⁄4 cup flour. Add the sugar mixture and toss to combine.
3. Spread the apples in the bottom of the prepared pie plate. Scatter the butter pieces over the apples. Sprinkle with the pecans and then the granulated sugar.
4. Roll the second disk of dough out on a lightly floured surface into an 11-inch round about 1⁄8 inch thick. Cut the dough into 1⁄2-inch-wide strips. Lay half of the strips 1 inch apart on the pie. Weave the remaining strips in the opposite direction to form a lattice. Press the edges to seal. Trim the overhang to 1⁄2 inch and fold it under itself. Crimp the edges with your fingers or a fork.
5. Bake the pie for about 45 minutes, until the crust is golden brown and the juices are bubbling. (If the crust is browning too quickly, cover the edges with foil.) Let cool on a wire rack for at least 4 hours before serving. Makes one 9-inch pie.
